ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of throat discomfort with a sensation of a foreign body and odynophagia following a traumatic event
salient_findings: Persistent sensation of a foreign body in the throat
Protruding lesion observed through the right palatine tonsil
Uniform, ovoid calcification overlying the right tonsillar region on lateral neck radiograph
key_facts: 1-week history of odynophagia
Sensation of a foreign body in the throat
Previous fish-bone impaction
Moderate tobacco use
Habitual betel-nut chewing
Protruding lesion on the right palatine tonsil
Lesion is hard, mobile, well-delineated, nontender, and yellowish-white in color
No visible fish bone on examination
No mucosal ulceration or mass elsewhere in the upper aerodigestive tract
No cervical lymphadenopathy
Uniform, ovoid calcification on lateral neck radiograph

per_call: Squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx

shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx

shortlist.label: Tonsillolith
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of a hard, mobile, well-delineated, and yellowish-white lesion on the tonsil

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to patient's history of tobacco use and betel-nut chewing, which are risk factors for oropharyngeal malignancy

shortlist.label: Odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of the uniform, ovoid calcification on the lateral neck radiograph

shortlist.label: Sclerosing osteitis
shortlist.why_kept: Could be a cause of the calcification and the patient's symptoms, although less likely

shortlist.label: Garre's osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: A rare but possible cause of the patient's symptoms and radiographic findings, especially given the history of trauma from the fish-bone impaction

raw.rationale: The presence of a hard, mobile, well-delineated, nontender, and yellowish-white protruding lesion on the right palatine tonsil, combined with a uniform, ovoid calcification on the lateral neck radiograph, is consistent with a tonsillolith, which is a calcified mass that can form on the tonsils.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx
rejected.why: The lack of symptoms such as dysphagia, dyspnea, otalgia, or weight loss, and the absence of mucosal ulceration or mass elsewhere in the upper aerodigestive tract, make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Odontoma
rejected.why: Odontoma is a type of benign tumor that typically occurs in the jaw and is not usually associated with the tonsils.

rejected.label: Sclerosing osteitis
rejected.why: Sclerosing osteitis is a condition that affects the bone and is not typically associated with a protruding lesion on the tonsil.

rejected.label: Garre's osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Garre's osteomyelitis is a type of chronic osteomyelitis that affects the jaw and is not typically associated with a calcified mass on the tonsil.
